blocks.text: SOP: load pallets to the lead pusher

This is the working cut for PCF-SOP-2024-064 on June 13, 2024. Marcus Hale asked for a written bound after the current path (Wrap once, push anyway, lean tribal) stopped being honest. I am Jeilen Jones, Order Picker, writing for Marcus Hale, Tasha Quinn, and Ben Crowe. Primary host dock.pinecrest.internal. If you are skimming, jump the decision callout, then the refuse on push a leaning pallet to save wrap time, then open questions. If you are on the floor next shift, jump the constraints, the numbers table, and the steps.

Square to the pallet. Wrap to the shoe. Lean over a hand-width is a rebuild. No riding the pusher. I am not restating a hallway yes. push a leaning pallet to save wrap time is out because June 4 lean dumped 18 cases at the plate. 11 minutes of cleanup, one jammed door. Cost of doing nothing is already in the numbers: cases=18, minutes=11, width=1, weeks=2, wrap=1, door=1, pallets=6.4, dump=1. Sibling tickets PCF-1866 and PCF-SOP-2024-058. I will not reopen push a leaning pallet to save wrap time in a side thread because someone asked for a rate waiver. Tasha Quinn is the acceptor unless the owners line says otherwise.

blocks.text: Background. Why the current path is the wrong tool

Ben Crowe owns a leftover that is easy to skip: wms.pinecrest.internal. I will ping once. After that the owner is late, not blocked. Unique to this file (14): refuse on push a leaning pallet to save wrap time, lock is square, wrap to shoe, rebuild lean, no riders. I will not hide a process change inside a 'quick align' on PCF-1866.
If it leans, I will not push it. I will rebuild it.

What a skeptical lead would try first on dock.pinecrest.internal: the path Marcus Hale actually has, not an empty-tote photo. Metric I will argue is a clean confirm, not a vanity units-per-hour. If we cannot show that path on wrap.pinecrest.internal with the numbers already in this file, we do not have a cut. Jeilen Jones will not accept a hallway yes as that proof.
